LD 1329 -- Ought Not to Pass

Joint Standing Committee on Transportation April 30, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the
Joint Standing Committee on Transportation, good morning. My name is
Alicia Rea, and I am a policy fellow for the American Civil Liberties Union
of Maine, a statewide organization committed to advancing and preserving
civil liberties guaranteed by the Maine and U.S. Constitutions. On behalf of
our members, Iurge you to oppose LD 1329.
This bill would require driver's licenses and nondriver identification cards to state whether the licensee or card holder is a citizen of the United States, a noncitizen of the United States or an asylum seeker.`
Under current law, "[t]he Secretary of State may not issue a license to an
applicant unless the applicant presents to the Secretary of State valid
documentary evidence of legal presence in the United States."2 By seeking
to add a requirement to Maine-issued identification cards and licenses, the legislation would do nothing more than label already vulnerable members of community.
The consequences of requiring a statement of citizenship on driver's
licenses and nondriver identification cards are potentially significant. State and local law enforcement, engaging in routine traffic enforcement, would be placed on alert to the immigration status of drivers and passengers in the course of their work. Retailers and restaurants would be notified of the immigration status of patrons while checking IDs for purchases of alcohol. Cannabis retailers would be on notice as to the status of their customers in purchases of products that are legal in Maine. Needlessly informing officials
and businesses of somebody's citizenship status when it is not legally
relevant is an invitation to discriminate.

In fact, under federal law, local law enforcement agencies are not required to hold anyone based on an ICE detainer alone? Since ICE detainers are not based on probable cause, state and local law enforcement agencies violate the Fourth Amendment when they hold a person solely on an immigration detainerf`

Unlike criminal warrants, which are supported by a judicial determination of probable cause, ICE detainers are issued by ICE enforcement agents without any authorization or oversight by a judge or other neutral decisionmaker. It is well settled that a person's presence in the United States in
violation of immigration laws on its own is not a crime. Immigration violations are generally civil, not criminal, in nature. As the United States
Supreme Court has explained, "[a]s a general rule, it is not a crime for a removable alien to remain present in the United States," and, thus, "[i]f the police stop someone based on nothing more than possible removability, the
usual predicate for an arrest is absent."5

Without the safeguards of a judicial warrant, ICE detainers have repeatedly resulted in the illegal detention of people who have not violated any
immigration laws and are not deportable, including United States citizens
and immigrants who are lawfully present in the United States. In fact, between 2008 and 2012 alone, ICE erroneously issued more than 800
detainers for United States citizens and over 28,000 for legal permanent
residents."

MEJ Testimony in opposition to LD 1329, An Act to Identify United States Citizenship Status on Driver's Licenses and Nondriver Identification Cards
April 28, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation. My name is Dina Malual and I am a Policy Advocate with Maine Equal Justice (MEJ), a nonprofit legal aid provider working to increase economic security, opportunity, and equity for people in Maine. Today we are testifying in opposition to LD 1329.
LD 1329 requires driver's licenses to indicate whether a driver is a U.S. citizen, noncitizen or an asylum seeker, which is not the purpose of said document. A driver's license is an official document that authorizes a person to operate a vehicle on public roads.
The marking of immigration status on driver's licenses is unnecessary and increases the risks of profiling, discrimination and overall fear among Maine's immigrant population. When obtaining a driver's license, an applicant must show proof of residency and citizenship or legal presence in the U.S.1 Asylum seekers are legally present in the U.S. for the purposes of obtaining a driver's license in Maine. The agencies that are required to note immigration status are already aware of its noncitizen applicants, meaning immigrant drivers in Maine have provided necessary documents verifying their lawful presence. LD 1329 does not provide important or new information.
Simply knowing the status of a person does nothing but subject them to profiling. At almost every point in an immigrant's life in Maine, they are perceived differently. We already know that Black and Brown people are subject to higher traffic stops and this bill will increase racial disparities by opening immigrants up to an additional layer of judgment.
1 https://www.maine.gov/sos/bmv/driver-licenses-and-ids/car-license/how-to-obtain-a-license

Considering there are many paths to immigration relief, we do not believe asylum seekers should be singled out. Furthermore, immigration status can change and this bill does not appropriately account for immigrants outside of the single status previously named.
For these reasons, we urge you to oppose LD 1329. Thank you for your consideration.

Testimony in Opposition to LD 1329, "An Act to Identify United States Citizenship Status on Driver's Licenses and Nondriver Identification Cards" James Myall, Senior Policy Analyst April 30, 2025
Good Afternoon, Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation. My name is James Myall, and I am a Senior Policy Analyst at the Maine Center for Economic Policy. I'm testifying today in opposition to LD 1329, "An Act to Identify United States Citizenship Status on Driver's Licenses and Nondriver Identification Cards." MECEP opposes LD 1329 because we believe it will add unnecessary information to state driver's licenses which risks discrimination, increasing fear among New Mainer communities, and ultimately harming our economy.
Driver's licenses are proof of your ability to drive. They are not immigration documents and they should not be made into immigration documents by this bill. Mainers have other ways of proving their immigration status through birth certificates, passports, and other documents issued by the federal government. We are concerned that adding immigration status to a driver's license will unnecessarily impact a driver's interactions with law enforcement agencies and other government entities.
Research shows that law enforcement officers can be prone to unfair treatment against immigrants or people they perceive as immigrants. We believe that even if an officer pulls someone over for an unrelated traffic offense, knowing the driver's immigration status could lead to harsher treatment for noncitizens. There are already documented examples of "citizenship profiling" among US police departments.i It also increases the likelihood that an officer will involve Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), even though a Maine driver's license cannot be obtained without lawful immigration status. There are similar risks for other government officials - would a general assistance officer view an application differently if an applicant presented a noncitizen driver's license as part of the application? We know that fear of police interactions leads to lower use of vital public benefits for some immigrants.ii
Finally, we are concerned that such a requirement will add to the existing atmosphere of fear among New Mainers. With several high profile incidents of people with lawful immigration status and even US citizenship being questioned, detained and deported by ICE, we believe that the requirement in this bill would lead some Mainers to forgo getting a drivers license or leaving the state entirely. Immigrants contribute to Maines economy by paying taxes, working in critical industries and starting businesses. We should be

welcoming them and helping them maximize their contributions - not putting a target on their backs. I urge you to vote ought not to pass on LD 1329. Thank you and I'm happy to take any questions.

Testimony of the Maine Immigrants' Rights Coalition (MIRC) In Opposition to LD 1329 An Act To Require Driver's Licenses and Nondriver Identification Cards To Indicate Citizenship or Immigration Status Public Hearing: April 30, 2025, 1:00 PM
Senator Nangel, Representative Crafts, and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation:
My name is Ruben Torres, and I serve as the Advocacy, Communications, and Policy Manager for the Maine Immigrants' Rights Coalition (MIRC). On behalf of our over 100 member organizations statewide, I am submitting this testimony inopposition to LD 1329, An Act To Require Driver's Licenses and Nondriver Identification Cards To Indicate Citizenship or Immigration Status.
Under existing statute, "The Secretary of State may not issue a license to an applicant unless the applicant presents... valid documentary evidence of legal presence in the United States." However, this bill proposes that driver's licenses and non-driver IDs should include a label indicating whether an individual is a U.S. citizen, a noncitizen, or an asylum seeker.
LD 1329 would add no new security benefit. Rather, it exposes individuals who have lawful presence under federal law to unnecessary scrutiny and potential harm by forcing a label on their license that may be misunderstood or misused.
By forcing people to carry a state-issued ID that marks them as a "noncitizen" or "asylum seeker," this legislation places a government stamp on what is, in effect, a profiling mechanism. We have deep concern about the downstream use of these licenses by employers, landlords, law enforcement, banks, or even school officials--none of whom are trained in immigration law, but all of whom might draw prejudicial or incorrect conclusions based on that label.
Immigration categories like "asylum seeker" are not fixed legal statuses--they often represent a stage in a legal process that can take years. There is a raised risk of mislabeling, either due to misunderstanding, outdated information, or flawed documentation. Once misidentified, individuals have no clear process for appeal or correction, raising serious due process concerns.
Our identification system should not be weaponized to mark or stigmatize. LD 1329 offers no public safety and instead subjects individuals to targeted discrimination. For these reasons, we urge the Committee to voteOught Not to Passon LD 1329. Thank you for your time and thoughtful consideration.
Respectfully,

Testimony of Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State and Cathie Curtis, Deputy Secretary for the Bureau of Motor Vehicles,
Department of the Secretary of State
April 30, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation,
I am providing testimony respectfully in opposition of L.D. 1329 "An Act to Identify United States
Citizenship Status on Driver's Licenses and Nondriver Identification Cards."
It has long been a widely held belief that a Mainer's license should indicate who they are, what types of
vehicles they are authorized to operate on our roads, and what restrictions are placed on their driving
privilege.

The federal govermnent has already started us down the slippery slope of using licenses for other
purposes with REAL ID, but Maine should not move itself further down that slope by requiring that
citizenship status be included on our driver licenses.

Even beyond these reasons to oppose L.D. 1329, I should note that this bill is additionally unnecessary for the sponsor's stated intent and would also be close to unworkable to accomplish those goals.
Only U.S. citizens may vote in our elections, but it is not a requirement that voters provide documentary proof of citizenship when registering to vote, which is why the sponsor's intent to provide voters an
identification document that connotes citizenship at the state level unnecessary.

If such a voter registration requirement were to become law, a requirement to include U.S. citizenship status on driver licenses would only be useful to Maine voters if they can access such a credential. Given
our current experience with Maine drivers coming in droves to get a REAL ID-compliant credential, we
would expect a flood of customers ahead of the subsequent election. Right now, we process about
300,000 license a year and there are approximately l million licenses. To handle the surge of customers
coming fora credential with their citizenship noted, we would need an additional 350 temporary staff for
branch offices (currently there are 100) and 70 temporary support staff in the administrative office
(currently 70), as well as two temporary HR generalists to hire all these people. We would also need
equipment, software licenses and other tools for these temporary hires to complete their work, as well as
additional appropriations for more leased space around the state.
